# How many Public Health Emergency of International Concern declarations have been made by WHO between 2009 and 2022?
## Community Answer
Between 2009 and 2022, the World Health Organization (WHO) has declared six Public Health **Emergency** of International Concern (PHEIC) declarations. The first PHEIC was declared in 2009 for the H1N1 **influenza pandemic** . The second PHEIC was declared in 2014 for the Ebola outbreak in West Africa.
The third PHEIC was declared in 2016 for the Zika virus outbreak. The fourth PHEIC was declared in January 2020 for the COVID-19 pandemic. The fifth PHEIC was declared in February 2021 due to the ongoing Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
The sixth PHEIC was declared in May 2021 due to the surge of COVID-19 cases in India and concerns about the emergence of new **variants** . In conclusion, WHO has declared six Public Health Emergency of International Concern declarations between 2009 and 2022.

...

## Explanation
**February 2021** : The fifth PHEIC addressed the ongoing Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, as it continued to threaten public health.
6. **May 2021** : The sixth PHEIC was declared concerning the surge of COVID-19 cases in India and the emergence of new variants.

# The 2024 Public Health Emergency of International Concern: A Global Failure to Control Mpox
## ABSTRACT.
On August 14, 2024, following a regional declaration by the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention, the World Health Organization declared mpox a Public Health Emergency of International Concern, marking the second such declaration in two years.

...

Between 2005 and 2023, the WHO declared eight PHEICs, namely H1N1 influenza (2009–2010); wild-type polio (2014–ongoing); Ebola (2013–2016 and 2018–2020); Zika neurologic syndromes (2015–2016); COVID-19 (2020–2023); and mpox (2022–2023 and 2024).
Encouragingly, in contrast to the arguably delayed declaration of the COVID-19 PHEIC, the 2024 mpox declaration ¹ was comparatively quick and decisive, as was the Global Health EDCTP3 call for proposals, releasing emergency funding for mpox outbreak research.
